title: Shadow escalation policy and graceful switchover for variant deploys
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Define and implement a deterministic 'shadow escalation' policy and graceful switchover flow for model variant deployments. The goal is to let teams run prolonged shadow experiments against production traffic, optionally escalate (promote) a variant to live for a subset of traffic based on multi-dimensional health signals, and provide an automatic, auditable rollback mechanism when regressions are detected.

Problem context: Current rollout primitives let us split traffic and run short canaries, but we lack a structured, auditable path from long-running shadowing -> staged promotion -> full rollout. This leads to manual, error-prone cutovers and delayed rollbacks when regressions surface only after minutes/hours of real traffic (semantic regressions, auth/rate-limit interactions, or rare tail latency issues). We also need to prioritize region and capacity tiers when deciding where to escalate, and ensure compatibility checks (tokenizer/schema/kv-cache compatibility) before promotion.

Proposed approach:
- Shadow Escalation Window: allow teams to define an evaluation window (eg. 1h, 4h, 24h) during which shadow metrics are aggregated.
- Composite Health Score: compute a composite signal combining: latency p50/p95, error rate (5xx/timeout), semantic regression score (batch eval on synthetic prompt set), functional failures (schema validation), and downstream quota/ratelimit errors. Weighting is configurable per-route.
- Promotion Policy: a policy spec that includes: minimum samples, health_score threshold, region affinity (preferred regions to promote in), capacity tier constraints (must have N free shards in dedicated), and canary slice size for staged promotion (eg. 1% -> 10% -> 50%).
- Proximity prioritization: when promoting, prefer same-region capacity first, then cross-region low-latency pairings, then spillback to lower-cost tiers only if policy allows.
- Compatibility gates: pre-promotion checks for tokenizer parity, schema hash match, kv-cache version compatibility. If any check fails, promotion is blocked and an automated issue is filed.
- Rollback Sentinels and Hysteresis: define per-promotion sentinels (eg. latency p95 + error rate + semantic delta) with hysteresis windows to avoid flapping. Automatic rollback triggers a staged drain and failover to previous variant with a cooldown (15m exponential backoff) and a post-mortem ticket template generated automatically.
- Audit and Explainability: every promotion/escalation decision must be recorded (policy input, score breakdown, sample requests that influenced semantic score), surfaced in Console, and linked to PR/Canary dashboard.

Implementation notes and tradeoffs:
- Semantic scoring requires sampled completions compared against golden prompts; this increases egress and compute cost. We will sample at a configurable rate and default to synthetic prompts from the route's eval-set.
- Compatibility gating must be fast (sub-second) to avoid blocking promotion pipelines; use precomputed model metadata (tokenizer fingerprint, schema fingerprint) stored in the model catalog.
- Multi-dimensional health scoring adds complexity; we will start with a simple weighted sum and provide a rules DSL for advanced teams.
- Promotion orchestration will reuse the existing deployment controller but add a 'shadow-escalator' sub-controller responsible for scoring, scheduling staged promotion slices, and invoking rollbacks.

Telemetry and metrics required:
- promotion_attempts_total, promotion_success_total, auto_rollback_total, composite_health_score{route,region,variant}, semantic_delta_samples, compatibility_block_count, promotion_latency_seconds.

acceptance_criteria:
1) Teams can create a Shadow Escalation policy in the Console/SDK and attach it to a deployment route.
2) System computes composite health score for shadow windows and shows score breakdown in Console.
3) 'Promote' orchestration runs staged promotions based on policy slices and honors region/capacity prioritization.
4) Compatibility gates block promotion when tokenizer/schema/kv-cache mismatch, and a clearly actionable error is shown.
5) Auto-rollback triggers when any sentinel breaches thresholds and performs graceful switchover to the previous variant within configured cooldown.
6) All promotion and rollback decisions are logged with score breakdown and sample traces and are queryable in the Console.
7) Unit and integration tests cover gating logic, promotion slices, and rollback hysteresis behavior.
notes_and_progress: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Eng, PM, and Design. Agreed composite score prototype and initial policy schema.
2026-02-19: Prototype scoring library merged to infra (PR #12345). Semantic scorer uses reservoir sampling + batch eval.
2026-02-24: Design reviewed mockups for Console UI. Design requested explicit 'why promoted' explainer and per-metric drilldowns.
2026-02-28: UX/PM requested a safety toggle to disable auto-promote for enterprise tenants by default. Need flagging in RBAC.
2026-03-03: Integration smoke tests in staging: successful staged promote 1%->10% in us-west-2 with no rollback. Observability wiring incomplete for semantic_delta metric.
review_feedback: PM (Jonah Li) 2026-02-24: Add customer impact matrix for promotion failures and a manual 'abort and capture' flow.
Design (Marisol Vega) 2026-02-24: Provide single-click rollback in the Console with reason capture. Include sample requests used for semantic scoring.
Security (Kira Novak) 2026-03-01: Ensure sampled payloads used for semantic scoring are redacted by default and compliant with PII policy.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for scoring weights and gating logic.
- End-to-end in staging: run long shadow on production traffic replay for 4h, validate scoreboard and automated promotion slices.
- Chaos test: induce p95 spikes in shadow variant and ensure auto-rollback triggers within defined hysteresis.
- Compliance test: validate redaction of sampled payloads.
deployment_plan:
Phase 1: Feature-flagged rollout to internal orgs only; expose simple policies and default conservative thresholds.
Phase 2: Enable for customer tenants with opt-in and RBAC controls.
Phase 3: Turn on enterprise defaults and add Console prompts for audit export.
postmortem_template:
- Incident summary
- Variant promoted and timeframe
- Triggering sentinel(s) and metric values
- Root cause analysis
- Remediation and follow-up tasks
